questions.q: Why did Yahweh instruct the people to select three cities?
questions.a: He instructed the people to select three cities so that everyone who kills another person could flee to one of them for safety.

questions.q: Why should the one who kills another flee to a safe city?
questions.a: He should flee so that the relative of the victim does not pursue him in anger and kill him.

questions.q: What provision does Yahweh make for the person who kills another person by accident?
questions.a: Yahweh provided three cities to which that person could flee and live.

questions.q: What would be the conditions for adding three more cities for people to escape to?
questions.a: If Yahweh enlarged their borders, then they must add three more cities for people to escape to.

questions.q: What should happen if a person ambushes and kills someone and then flees to one of these cities?
questions.a: The elders of this man’s city must bring him back and turn him over to the victim’s relative so that the attacker may be executed.

questions.q: How many witnesses are needed for someone to be punished for their sin?
questions.a: There must be two or three witnesses for anyone to be punished for their sin.

questions.q: What should be done when controversy exists between two men?
questions.a: Then the two men who have a controversy must go before the priests and the judges who are serving at that time. The judges will inquire thoroughly to see if the witness falsely testified against the other.

questions.q: What must be done if a witness is found to be false?
questions.a: If the testimony of a witness is found to be false, then they must do to him as he had planned to do to the person he accused.

commentary.text: The cities of refuge, The man-slayer, The murderer.

Verses 1–13 Here is the law settled between the blood of the murdered, and the blood of the murderer; provision is made, that the cities of refuge should be a protection, so that a man should not die for that as a crime, which was not his willing act. In Christ, the Lord our Righteousness, refuge is provided for those who by faith flee unto him. But there is no refuge in Jesus Christ for presumptuous sinners, who go on still in their trespasses. Those who flee to Christ from their sins, shall be safe in him, but not those who expect to be sheltered by him in their sins.

Direction is given to fix landmarks in Canaan. It is the will of God that every one should know his own; and that means should be used to hinder the doing and suffering of wrong. This, without doubt, is a moral precept, and still binding. Let every man be content with his own lot, and be just to his neighbours in all things.

Sentence should never be passed upon the testimony of one witness alone. A false witness should suffer the same punishment which he sought to have inflicted upon the person he accused. Nor could any law be more just. Let all Christians not only be cautious in bearing witness in public, but be careful not to join in private slanders; and let all whose consciences accuse them of crime, without delay flee for refuge to the hope set before them in Jesus Christ.
